```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  comment = "#>", collapse = TRUE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dpi = 120

```

**Box score totals reward teams that play fast and players who play a lot.
Advanced metrics strip those effects out by measuring per possession and per
shot.** This article computes the standard set (possessions, pace, offensive and
defensive rating, the four factors, effective field goal percentage, true
shooting and usage) from the season box scores that `wehoop` publishes, with
every formula written out as `dplyr` code you can read and change.

Everything here runs offline on pre-built release files, so it is quick and
does not touch a live API. If you are new to `wehoop`, start with
[Getting Started](getting-started-wehoop.html), whose glossary defines each term.

## What you'll learn

- How to estimate possessions from a box score, and how good the estimate is.
- How to compute pace, offensive, defensive and net rating.
- How to compute Dean Oliver's four factors for offense and defense.
- How to compute eFG%, TS% and usage rate for players.
- How the same code runs on women's college basketball.

`wehoop` does not ship helper functions for these formulas, so we write them out.
That is deliberate here: seeing the formula is the point.

```{r libraries}
library(wehoop)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Load the box scores

We use the 2025 WNBA regular season (`season_type == 2`).

```{r load}
team_box <- load_wnba_team_box(seasons = 2025) |>
  filter(season_type == 2)
player_box <- load_wnba_player_box(seasons = 2025) |>
  filter(season_type == 2)
```

ESPN files the All-Star Game as a regular-season game between two one-off
teams. Keep only the franchises, which each played a full schedule.

```{r franchises}
franchises <- team_box |>
  count(team_id) |>
  filter(n >= 20) |>
  pull(team_id)

team_box <- team_box |> filter(team_id %in% franchises)
player_box <- player_box |> filter(team_id %in% franchises)

length(franchises)
```

## Possessions

A possession ends when the team on offense makes a shot, loses the ball, or
the defense rebounds a miss. Box scores do not count possessions, so we estimate
them:

$$
\text{Poss} = \text{FGA} - \text{OREB} + \text{TOV} + 0.44 \times \text{FTA}
$$

Field goal attempts start possessions, offensive rebounds extend one (so they
are subtracted), turnovers end one without a shot, and 0.44 converts free throw
attempts to the trips to the line that end a possession (a two-shot foul is one
trip; and-ones and technicals are not trips).

Use `total_turnovers`, which includes team turnovers such as shot-clock
violations; `turnovers` counts only those charged to a player.

Each team-game row needs its opponent's stats too (for defensive measures), so
join each row to its mirror row from the same game.

```{r possessions}
games <- team_box |>
  transmute(
    game_id, team_id, team = team_abbreviation, team_score,
    fga = field_goals_attempted, fgm = field_goals_made,
    fg3m = three_point_field_goals_made, fg3a = three_point_field_goals_attempted,
    fta = free_throws_attempted, ftm = free_throws_made,
    oreb = offensive_rebounds, dreb = defensive_rebounds,
    tov = total_turnovers,
    poss = fga - oreb + tov + 0.44 * fta
  )

games <- games |>
  inner_join(
    games |> rename_with(~ paste0("opp_", .x), -game_id),
    by = "game_id",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  filter(team_id != opp_team_id)

games |>
  select(game_id, team, poss, opp_team, opp_poss) |>
  head()
```

The two teams' estimates in a game differ slightly, because the formula is an
approximation. A common refinement averages them so both teams share one
possession count.

### How good is the estimate?

The WNBA Stats API play-by-play lets you count possessions directly.
`load_wnba_stats_possessions()` publishes one row per counted possession from a
GitHub release, so we can compare the box score estimate with the count. The two
sources use different game ids, so compare the league average per team-game
rather than game by game.

```{r validate}
counted <- load_wnba_stats_possessions(seasons = 2025) |>
  # regular-season WNBA Stats game ids start with "102"
  filter(substr(game_id, 1, 3) == "102", count_as_possession == TRUE)

poss_check <- tibble(
  source = c("Box score estimate", "Counted from play-by-play"),
  possessions_per_team_game = c(
    mean(games$poss),
    nrow(counted) / (2 * length(unique(counted$game_id)))
  )
)
poss_check
```

For 2025 the box score estimate runs about
`r round(100 * (poss_check$possessions_per_team_game[1] / poss_check$possessions_per_team_game[2] - 1), 1)`%
above the play-by-play count. Part of the gap is definitional: the 0.44
free-throw weight is a league-average constant that was fitted to men's
professional basketball, and the counted file applies its own rules to
end-of-period and free-throw edge cases. The counted file may also include
exhibition games filed as regular-season games, so treat this as a sanity check
rather than an exact reconciliation. For ratings, the gap mostly cancels:
offensive and defensive rating share the same denominator.

## Pace

Pace is possessions per 40 minutes. Overtime adds minutes, so divide by the
minutes actually played. Team minutes come from the player box score: five
players are always on the court, so team minutes are the players' minutes
divided by five.

$$
\text{Pace} = 40 \times \frac{(\text{Poss} + \text{Opp Poss}) / 2}{\text{Team minutes} / 5}
$$

```{r minutes}
team_minutes <- player_box |>
  group_by(game_id, team_id) |>
  summarise(team_min = sum(minutes, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

games <- games |> left_join(team_minutes, by = c("game_id", "team_id"))

summary(games$team_min)
```

Minutes are rounded to whole numbers per player, so a 40-minute game sums to
about 200.

## Offensive, defensive and net rating

$$
\text{ORtg} = 100 \times \frac{\text{PTS}}{\text{Poss}}, \qquad
\text{DRtg} = 100 \times \frac{\text{Opp PTS}}{\text{Poss}}, \qquad
\text{Net} = \text{ORtg} - \text{DRtg}
$$

Sum the season totals first, then divide. Averaging per-game ratings would
weight a 65-possession game the same as an 80-possession one.

```{r ratings}
team_season <- games |>
  mutate(avg_poss = (poss + opp_poss) / 2) |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(
    games = n(),
    wins = sum(team_score > opp_team_score),
    pts = sum(team_score), opp_pts = sum(opp_team_score),
    poss = sum(avg_poss),
    minutes = sum(team_min),
    across(c(fga, fgm, fg3m, fta, ftm, oreb, dreb, tov,
             opp_fga, opp_fgm, opp_fg3m, opp_fta, opp_ftm, opp_oreb, opp_dreb, opp_tov),
           sum),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    win_pct = wins / games,
    pace = 40 * poss / (minutes / 5),
    ortg = 100 * pts / poss,
    drtg = 100 * opp_pts / poss,
    net = ortg - drtg
  )

team_season |>
  select(team, games, win_pct, pace, ortg, drtg, net) |>
  arrange(desc(net))
```

```{r net-vs-wins, fig.alt = "Scatter plot of 2025 WNBA teams with net rating on the x-axis and winning percentage on the y-axis."}
ggplot(team_season, aes(net, win_pct)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "grey70", formula = y ~ x) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#221A4D") +
  geom_text(aes(label = team), vjust = -0.9, size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "2025 WNBA: net rating and winning percentage",
    x = "Net rating (points per 100 possessions)", y = "Winning percentage",
    caption = "Data: wehoop::load_wnba_team_box()"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r net-cor}
cor(team_season$net, team_season$win_pct)
```

## The four factors

Dean Oliver identified four things that decide most games, each measured for a
team's offense and the same quantity allowed on defense:

| Factor | Offense | Defense |
|---|---|---|
| Shooting | $\text{eFG\%} = \frac{\text{FGM} + 0.5 \times \text{3PM}}{\text{FGA}}$ | the opponent's eFG% |
| Turnovers | $\text{TOV\%} = \frac{\text{TOV}}{\text{Poss}}$ | the opponent's TOV% |
| Offensive rebounding | $\text{OREB\%} = \frac{\text{OREB}}{\text{OREB} + \text{Opp DREB}}$ | $\text{DREB\%} = \frac{\text{DREB}}{\text{DREB} + \text{Opp OREB}}$ |
| Free throws | $\text{FT rate} = \frac{\text{FTM}}{\text{FGA}}$ | the opponent's FT rate |

Some sources define FT rate as FTA / FGA, which measures getting to the line
rather than converting there. Oliver's version, FTM / FGA, is used below.

```{r four-factors}
four_factors <- team_season |>
  mutate(
    efg = (fgm + 0.5 * fg3m) / fga,
    tov_pct = tov / poss,
    oreb_pct = oreb / (oreb + opp_dreb),
    ft_rate = ftm / fga,
    opp_efg = (opp_fgm + 0.5 * opp_fg3m) / opp_fga,
    opp_tov_pct = opp_tov / poss,
    dreb_pct = dreb / (dreb + opp_oreb),
    opp_ft_rate = opp_ftm / opp_fga
  ) |>
  select(team, net, efg, tov_pct, oreb_pct, ft_rate,
         opp_efg, opp_tov_pct, dreb_pct, opp_ft_rate) |>
  arrange(desc(net))

four_factors |>
  mutate(across(-team, ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

Which factor tracks winning most closely this season? Correlate each team's
factor margin (offense minus what it allowed) with net rating. With only
`r nrow(team_season)` teams this is descriptive, not a model.

```{r factor-cor}
four_factors |>
  transmute(
    net,
    shooting = efg - opp_efg,
    turnovers = opp_tov_pct - tov_pct,
    rebounding = oreb_pct - (1 - dreb_pct),
    free_throws = ft_rate - opp_ft_rate
  ) |>
  summarise(across(-net, ~ cor(.x, net))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "factor_margin", values_to = "cor_with_net")
```

Signs are arranged so that a positive margin is good for the team in every row.

## Player efficiency: eFG%, TS% and usage

**True shooting percentage** folds free throws into shooting efficiency. Each
true shot attempt is a field goal attempt or a free throw trip (0.44 of an FTA):

$$
\text{TS\%} = \frac{\text{PTS}}{2 \times (\text{FGA} + 0.44 \times \text{FTA})}
$$

**Usage rate** is the share of team possessions a player finishes, by a shot, a
trip to the line or a turnover, while she is on the court:

$$
\text{USG\%} = 100 \times
\frac{(\text{FGA} + 0.44 \times \text{FTA} + \text{TOV}) \times (\text{Team MIN} / 5)}
     {\text{MIN} \times (\text{Team FGA} + 0.44 \times \text{Team FTA} + \text{Team TOV})}
$$

Usage needs the team totals from the games the player played, so join each
player-game to its team-game row first.

```{r player-metrics}
team_game_totals <- games |>
  select(game_id, team_id, team_min, team_fga = fga, team_fta = fta, team_tov = tov)

players <- player_box |>
  filter(did_not_play == FALSE, !is.na(minutes), minutes > 0) |>
  inner_join(team_game_totals, by = c("game_id", "team_id")) |>
  group_by(athlete_display_name, team_abbreviation) |>
  summarise(
    games = n(),
    min = sum(minutes),
    pts = sum(points),
    fga = sum(field_goals_attempted), fgm = sum(field_goals_made),
    fg3m = sum(three_point_field_goals_made),
    fta = sum(free_throws_attempted),
    tov = sum(turnovers),
    team_min = sum(team_min),
    team_used = sum(team_fga + 0.44 * team_fta + team_tov),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    efg = (fgm + 0.5 * fg3m) / fga,
    ts = pts / (2 * (fga + 0.44 * fta)),
    usage = 100 * (fga + 0.44 * fta + tov) * (team_min / 5) / (min * team_used)
  )

players |>
  filter(min >= 500) |>
  arrange(desc(usage)) |>
  select(athlete_display_name, team_abbreviation, games, min, pts, efg, ts, usage) |>
  head(12)
```

```{r usage-ts-plot, fig.alt = "Scatter plot of 2025 WNBA players with at least 500 minutes, usage rate on the x-axis and true shooting percentage on the y-axis."}
qualified <- players |> filter(min >= 500)

ggplot(qualified, aes(usage, ts)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "#7c689c") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = athlete_display_name),
    data = qualified |> filter(usage > quantile(usage, 0.93) | ts > quantile(ts, 0.97)),
    size = 3, vjust = -0.8, check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "2025 WNBA: usage and true shooting (500+ minutes)",
    x = "Usage rate (%)", y = "True shooting",
    caption = "Data: wehoop::load_wnba_player_box(), wehoop::load_wnba_team_box()"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Players in the top-right carry a large share of the offense and stay efficient,
which is hard to sustain.

## Women's college basketball

The college box scores have the same columns, so the code carries over. Division
I teams also play non-Division I opponents, so restrict the table to teams with
a full schedule in the release.

```{r wbb}
wbb_box <- load_wbb_team_box(seasons = 2026) |>
  filter(season_type %in% c(2, 3))

wbb_games <- wbb_box |>
  transmute(
    game_id, team_id, team = team_location, team_score,
    fga = field_goals_attempted, fgm = field_goals_made,
    fg3m = three_point_field_goals_made, fta = free_throws_attempted,
    oreb = offensive_rebounds, tov = total_turnovers,
    poss = fga - oreb + tov + 0.44 * fta
  )

wbb_games <- wbb_games |>
  inner_join(wbb_games |> select(game_id, opp_team_id = team_id,
                                 opp_score = team_score, opp_poss = poss),
             by = "game_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(team_id != opp_team_id)

wbb_games |>
  mutate(avg_poss = (poss + opp_poss) / 2) |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(
    games = n(),
    ortg = 100 * sum(team_score) / sum(avg_poss),
    drtg = 100 * sum(opp_score) / sum(avg_poss),
    efg = (sum(fgm) + 0.5 * sum(fg3m)) / sum(fga),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(games >= 25) |>
  mutate(net = ortg - drtg) |>
  arrange(desc(net)) |>
  head(10)
```

These are raw ratings: they do not account for who a team played. A team that
beats weak opponents by 40 looks better here than it is. The
[team ratings model](womens-college-basketball-team-ratings-model.html) adjusts
for schedule strength.

## Official numbers for a single game

The WNBA Stats API publishes its own advanced box scores per game, computed from
counted possessions. They make a useful check on your formulas. These are live
calls to stats.wnba.com, so they are not run here.

```{r official, eval = FALSE}
wnba_boxscorefourfactorsv3(game_id = "1022500001")
wnba_boxscoreadvancedv3(game_id = "1022500001")
wnba_boxscoreusagev3(game_id = "1022500001")
```
